Approach 1: Direct Correlation & Approach 1 directly relates the in vitro and in vivo times associated with the same response values after preprocessing (i.e., in vivo time is modeled as a function of in vitro time). When the datasets do not contain the same response values, the app can interpolate time at shared response values to create the paired times used for fitting. The fitted model is then used as a time-scaling function that maps an in vitro time to a predicted in vivo time.

This approach can be useful when the main question is how the time required to reach a given response in vitro corresponds to the time required to reach that response in vivo. & Double Exponential, Exponential, Linear, Linear (zero intercept), Power \\
Approach 2: Independent Model Fitting & Approach 2 fits the same model family (e.g., exponential decay) separately to the preprocessed observed in vitro and in vivo datasets. The two datasets do not need matching time points or response values, so interpolation is not used for Approach 2 fitting. With fitting data alone, the report summarizes the two fitted models and uncertainty for those fitted curves. When prediction data are supplied, predictions can be generated by comparing the fitted in vivo and in vitro responses or by comparing fitted characteristic time constants when those values are available.

This approach can be useful when the two datasets were measured on different time schedules, when each dataset is expected to follow the same type of degradation curve, or when a specific model form is scientifically meaningful for both datasets. & Double Exponential, Exponential, Mass Loss (Gompertz), Mass Loss (Gompertz, Normalized), Mass Loss (One-Phase), Mass Loss (One-Phase, Normalized), Mass Loss (Surface Erosion), Mass Loss (Surface Erosion, Normalized), Mass Loss (Two-Phase), Mass Loss (Two-Phase, Normalized), Power, Stretched Exponential \\
Approach 3: Direct Mapping & Approach 3 uses direct interpolation-based mappings between datasets rather than fitting a parametric model. Response values interpolated at shared times are used for response-value ratios over time, while times interpolated at shared response values are used for time ratios across response-value ranges. When prediction data are supplied, those mappings can be used to map in vitro response values or in vitro times to the corresponding in vivo response values or times.

This approach can be useful for exploratory comparisons, for datasets where a simple equation does not describe the observed pattern well, or when the user wants a direct data-based mapping rather than a fitted model. & No parametric model selection \\
